newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as yen surges.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end weak as yen surges.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Wednesday as players sold export-related shares in the underlying cash market on the back of the yen's strong gains.
Nikkei 225 June futures ended 260 points lower at 20,325 after hitting an early high of 20,650. September was more actively traded and finished 265 points lower at 20,365.
Dealers said the market could head below the key 20,000 level if the yen continued to strengthen.
"The yen is tearing the stock market apart. I hope the psychological level of 20,000 can hold. Otherwise confidence will be very badly affected," a trader at a local house said.
The dollar slumped to its lowest levels in almost seven months against the yen on concerns a burgeoning Japanese current account surplus would fuel trade tensions between the U.S. and Japan.
A chartist with another local brokerage said the Nikkei futures market looked set to head lower.
He said the September contract, the new lead month after June's expiry on Thursday, faced support around 20,160 but a breach of that level could push it well below 20,000.
"If September holds above 20,170-20,200, there's a likelihood we'll see more of an uptrend but it won't be a strong one," he said, adding that the market faced resistance around 20,470-20,520.
In Taiwan futures, the June contract ended at 351.8 against its opening 355.5 on volume of 796 lots.
